_README: The kit's blessed versions, and the conditions under which each one applies.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: the kit is a platform. It ships configs, CI jobs and a
library standard, and a platform that asserts a tool has to pin it — otherwise
every project answers 'which version do we run?' on its own and the fleet
silently diverges. The rule is one line:
THE KIT PINS WHAT THE KIT SHIPS, OR WHAT THE KIT'S CHOICES DRAG IN.
That second clause is not decoration. `zod` is nobody's declared dependency in
some repos and is still the sharpest version trap in this stack, because
better-auth needs v4 while drizzle-kit and shadcn pull v3 — and the loser of
that hoist fails at RUNTIME, not at build.
Anything the kit says nothing about stays the project's own call, handled by
Dependabot and the dependency-triage pass. This file is not a list of every
dependency; it is the list the kit refuses to let drift.
EXACT VERSIONS, NOT RANGES. A caret lets a fresh install drift to a version the
kit never blessed, defeating lockstep silently — and `npm install` ADDS a caret
by default, which is how it keeps coming back. `whenResolved` entries are the
exception and pin a MAJOR, because a transitively-dragged package's exact
version is not the project's to choose.
EACH ENTRY CARRIES ITS OWN TRIGGER, and the trigger is what makes 'opinionated
but does not block unless it matters' mechanical rather than a convention:
applies: 'whenDeclared'        this project declares it -> it must be ours
applies: {whenFile: [...]}     a kit-shipped config is present -> the tool
behind it must be pinned. No config, no opinion.
applies: 'whenResolved'        it is anywhere in the lockfile, transitive
included -> one major across the whole tree.
severity: 'required'           a violation fails the build
severity: 'advisory'           a violation prints and passes — for a real
problem the fleet has not adopted the fix for yet
installedBy: 'project'         a declared dependency; the guard checks package.json
installedBy: 'ci'              installed by a workflow at run time; this file owns
the version and CI reads it, so no project declares it
ENFORCEMENT is scripts/check-stack.mjs (CI job `stack-standard`) — hermetic,
reads manifests and the lockfile, never the network.
`blessed_at` is the date of the last full TanStack review. Entries added since
carry their own `blessedAt`, so one date never claims a review that did not happen.
MOVING A PIN is /review-stack: read what changed between our version and latest,
decide whether it affects how WE use it, and update whatever references it
invalidates. Never bump this file to make a build pass.

better-auth.why: Better Auth holds the front door, and its breaking changes are invisible until a version boundary. 1.7 made `issuer` a REQUIRED field on the account model and made sign-in filter on it: a project whose authaccount table predates that column has the field read as undefined, the filter never matches, and EVERY sign-in fails as "Invalid email or password" with the user, the account and the password hash all verifiably correct. A caret range walks a project across that boundary on a fresh install with no commit to blame. Pin exactly; treat an upgrade as a change that needs the auth tables re-checked against @better-auth/core's own schema definitions.

@biomejs/biome.why: The kit ships biome.json AND a CI biome job, so the kit owns the linter. biome.json's $schema names a version; a different binary reads that config as something else. Worse, a project that declares nothing at all gets `npx biome` resolving to an UNRELATED package of that name on npm which exits 0 — a lint gate that passes without linting, locally and on a runner.

@commitlint/cli.why: commitlint.yml installs this at run time. Unpinned, that executes whatever the registry serves under the name, and --no-save leaves no record of what ran. This file owns the version and the guard asserts the workflow names it, so the two cannot drift apart.

@commitlint/config-conventional.why: commitlint.yml installs this at run time. Unpinned, that executes whatever the registry serves under the name, and --no-save leaves no record of what ran. This file owns the version and the guard asserts the workflow names it, so the two cannot drift apart.

_form_rule: Form-library adoption is decided PER APP, all-in within an app. Three states,
and the third is a hard failure:
1. app declares @tanstack/react-form           -> decided, nothing to record
2. app listed in FORM_LIB_EXEMPT_APPS          -> deliberately decided no
3. app in neither                              -> question never asked, FAIL
FORM_LIB_EXEMPT_APPS is a space-separated app-name list in
.claude/sync-substitutions.json, read at runtime (same shape as DEPLOY_WORKFLOWS).
Exempt suits apps with no real data entry — ecommerce/cart surfaces, marketing
pages, and control-plane/service apps whose UI is a couple of status screens.
Data-entry apps (ERP browses and record forms) take the library.

_references_notes: DISTILLED, not copied. Our subset in our words, scoped to what business
applications need. `distilled_from` records which upstream skills were read, so
/review-stack knows what to re-read when a pin moves; an empty list means
there is no upstream for it.
NOT CARRIED, deliberately: every migrate-* skill (one-offs — SKILL.md says where
to read one), server-components (we do not use RSC), offline persistence,
SCOPE RULE: if we do not use a feature, it does not get pages explaining how the
feature works. Upstream already documents it and node_modules already has it.

start-middleware.why: We deliberately do NOT use createMiddleware for auth (server-functions.md). #2783 — server middleware in the client bundle — was open Nov 2024 to Feb 2026. Still open: #7213 (middleware calling a server function in another file throws) and #7459 (createMiddleware undefined on cold-start SSR in vite dev, filed against 1.168.9).
start-middleware.action: If both close, the technical objection is gone — but the decision still needs a reason to adopt beyond saving lines. Middleware's only real capability over a handler-top call is running code AFTER the handler. Re-open only when something genuinely needs wrapping.

_why: they are NOT equally load-bearing — measured across the fleet, not assumed:
1. THE APP DECLARES THE MAJOR ITSELF (required).
Vite inlines better-auth into dist/server/server.js, and the inlined
`import 'zod'` resolves from the APP's directory. An app with its own
nested v4 gets v4 no matter what is hoisted to the root. All 7 Vite apps
across the 3 projects declare zod ^4.4.3, and all 3 root hoists differ
(v3, v3 and v4) with no production failure anywhere.
This half is what makes the root hoist irrelevant.
Belt and braces for a hoist change that has not happened. 6 of the 7 apps
do not carry it and run in production, so it is ROBUSTNESS, not
correctness — and a check that failed them would be wrong, not strict.
